raw_response:
I would keep the usual North China Plain pattern and plant a winter wheat and summer maize rotation on most of my land. I am in Quzhou County, Hebei, so this fits the local climate, my experience, and the irrigation conditions best. At 54 years old with primary education, I would choose a simple plan I can manage steadily rather than something risky or complicated. I would use improved or hybrid seed because I care about stable yield and easier field management more than saving a little on seed. For wheat, I would focus on base fertilizer, one or two topdressings of nitrogen, careful spring watering, and disease and aphid control if pressure shows up. For summer maize, I would plant quickly after wheat harvest, use enough fertilizer early, irrigate when the field turns dry, and control weeds and insects in time. I would use rotary tillage for convenience after harvest and sowing, because it is faster and suits a wheat-maize rotation.
